text:
Maya Li: heads up — encountered weird auth/retry behavior in the Next.js edge starter using the browser SDK + LlamaIndex demo. Streaming chat starts then stalls and we see repeated 401s in the server logs. Repro steps below. @Leo @Priya

Leo Nguyen: can you paste the minimal repro and env?

Maya Li: repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/dev-starters.git branch `next-edge-browser-sdk`. Steps: `pnpm i`, `pnpm dev`, open `/examples/llama-chat`, send a prompt. Env: Node 18.16, next@13.4.7, @redwood/browser-sdk@0.4.0, @redwood/sdk@0.8.0 (server). Behavior: client tries refresh during stream, server rejects then client retries and we get token-flip loops. Logs: 

```
Client -> /api/stream (with browser token)
Server: 401 { error: 'token_expired' }
Client: fetch /auth/refresh -> 200 { token: 'xxx' }
Client -> /api/stream (reconnect) -> 401
Server: 401 { error: 'invalid_grant' }
Client: fetch /auth/refresh -> 200 { token: 'yyy' }
...repeats...
```

Maya Li: streaming reconnect codepath uses the browser-sdk auto-refresh which assumes the server will accept the new token immediately. But on our auth backend refresh returns a token that needs a tiny propagation window in Dedicated deployments. That race + retry logic in browser-sdk means repeated 401s and a bad UX.

Priya Rao: interesting. Two axes: 1) SDK parity — browser vs node should share the same retry semantics, 2) starter app should include resilience (backoff + one-time retry) and doc notes.

Leo Nguyen: workaround for now: set `autoRefresh: false` in browser-sdk and handle refresh on server side, or add a 200ms backoff before reconnect. Quick patch: 

```js
// client
const client = new BrowserClient({ autoRefresh: false });
// server-side endpoint handles refresh-on-401 and returns 202 to client while it waits
```

Maya Li: I'll add a tiny note in the example README and a helper util for server-proxied refresh. Also created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dev-starters/issues/77 to track.

infra-bot: CI run 2201 started for branch next-edge-browser-sdk :gear:

Priya Rao: longer term: SDK should expose `retryPolicy` that supports `single_retry`, `backoff_ms`, and a `tokenCompare` hook so clients can avoid retrying if refresh produced the same token string. Also need a unit test in eval-harness to simulate refresh propagation delays.

Leo Nguyen: agreed. I'll prototype `tokenCompare` in the node SDK first then port to browser SDK. Also adding a gating e2e that runs the llamaindex chat flow in CI with short token TTL to catch flakiness.

Maya Li: PR opened for docs + starter fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dev-starters/pull/89 — includes example server refresh helper and README troubleshooting.

Priya Rao: opened SDK issue to track parity work: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/412 — labeling `dx/priority`.

Leo Nguyen: I'll push a small SDK patch that adds `retryPolicy: { on401: 'single' }` default for streaming until we have better propagation handling.

Maya Li: thanks both. if CI shows the e2e failing I'll revert the browser auto-refresh to false in the starter so new users don't hit it.

infra-bot: CI run 2201 completed — e2e reported flaky in /examples/llama-chat (1 failure) :warning:

Maya Li: filing a follow-up to add flaky e2e tag + retry in CI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dev-starters/issues/78 :memo:
